pages.exclusionReason: Title, objectives/contents roadmap or closing thanks, without independent technical exposition.

observations: Printed3 Contents repeats the six topic areas and says other concepts are discussed in their corresponding lectures; no independent mathematical exposition.
pages.exclusionReason: Title, objectives/contents roadmap or closing thanks, without independent technical exposition.

observations: Printed4 Vectors: ordered sequence, typically a column in robotics; component addition, scalar multiplication, dot product withcosθ, Euclidean norm sqrt(sum squares)=sqrt(x^Tx). Three-link drawing places red position vectorp from fixed origin to tipP with column[xtip,ytip].
meaningfulAngles: Vector ordering, column convention and position coordinates relative to a fixed frame rather than joint count.
Componentwise vector addition and scalar multiplication.
Dot product, angle and Euclidean norm interpretation/calculation.

observations: Printed5 Matrices: mrows,ncolumns and explicit3×3index layout; transpose swaps indices/rows/columns; identity diagonal1/offdiagonal0 andAI=A; symmetricA=A^T; robotic mass distribution/inertia tensor application.
meaningfulAngles: Matrix dimensions/indexing and transpose.
Identity and symmetry definitions/recognition.
Matrix representation of rigid-link mass distribution and inertia for dynamics.

observations: Printed6 Skew symmetryS=−S^T withzero diagonal; displayedcross-product matrix has signs[0,−Ωz,Ωy;Ωz,0,−Ωx;−Ωy,Ωx,0] andΩ×P=SP. Multiplication inner dimensions, associativity, generally noncommutativity, transformation-chain/DH application.
meaningfulAngles: Skew symmetry, diagonal restriction, and signed cross-product matrix.
Matrix multiplication dimension compatibility, output dimensions, associativity versus order.
Composing robot transformations to obtain end-effector pose.

observations: Printed7 Determinant scalar for square matrix, linear-transformation scale; rank independent rows/columns; inverse iffdetnonzero,AAinverse=I, inverse=adj(A)/detA. Jacobian rank loss called singularity; detJ=0 applies only squareJ. Final target-joint-angle bullet is an application, not proof that pose-to-joints is ordinary matrix inversion.
meaningfulAngles: Determinant/rank/invertibility distinctions and singular square-Jacobian consequences.
Adjugate-over-determinant inverse formula and identity check.
Determinant as geometric scaling factor, with square-matrix domain.

observations: Printed8 Eigenvector must be nonzero and satisfyAx=λx; characteristicdet(λI−A)=0; directions andscaling interpretation. Negative real parts of all system eigenvalues gives asymptotic stability for the implicit continuous-time linear system, not arbitrary nonlinear/discrete systems.
meaningfulAngles: Eigenvalue/eigenvector definition, nonzero-vector condition, characteristic equation and computation.
Geometric eigen-direction/scaling interpretation.
Negative-real-part stability criterion with continuous-time linear assumption.

observations: Printed9 Scalarf:R^n→R; gradient column ofpartials. Artificial-potential-field plot axesX/Y, greenGoal near(6,6), redObstacle near(−2,−2); high contours aroundobstacle, lower near goal, inset magnifies obstacle. Text describes goal attraction andobstacle repulsion.
meaningfulAngles: Gradient scalar-to-vector shape and partial derivative calculation.
Potential-field goal attraction versus obstacle repulsion and high/low contours; distinguish gradient from downhill direction if stated.

observations: Printed10 Derivatives of time-varying vectors/matrices are elementwise;A dot=[d aij/dt]. Position/orientation vary withtime. Rdot=S(ω)R, whereSskew andωangular velocity; left multiplication requires compatible reference-frame convention.
meaningfulAngles: Elementwise vector/matrix time derivatives.
Rotation derivativeRdot=S(ω)R and skew angular-velocity matrix, with convention-aware multiplication order.

observations: Printed11 Probability foundations: trial/experiment, sample space Ω, countable versus uncountable outcomes. Bounds use P(X≤xi), while the discrete normalization uses sum P(X=xi)=1; these are different probability functions. Diagram legend: blue robot, green available, red blocked, black walls. Four available neighboring states each show0.25, rather than assigning mass to the robot or blocked cells.
meaningfulAngles: Experiment/sample space and discrete versus continuous outcomes.
Probability bounds and normalization without confusing cumulative and mass probabilities.
Diagram legend, available versus blocked states and normalized equiprobable available moves.

observations: Printed12 Conditional probability and Bayes: P(A|B)=P(B|A)P(A)/P(B); prior before evidence and posterior afterward. LocalizationP(x|z) from noisy measurements. Speech decodingP(i|o)=P(o|i)P(i)/P(o), whereiword sequence andoaudio.
meaningfulAngles: Bayes factor roles, nonzero evidence denominator and posterior computation.
Prior versus posterior and conditioning direction.
Localization and speech-decoding applications of the same conditional structure.

observations: Printed13 Random variable maps outcomes Ω to real numbers. Expectation sum xiP(X=xi) for discrete, integral xfX(x) over real line for continuous. PMF versus PDF named. Weighted expected reward is the robotics/Q-learning motivation, not a full Q-update formula.
meaningfulAngles: Random-variable definition and sample outcome versus numerical value.
PMF versus PDF and discrete versus continuous expectation formulas.
Expected reward as probability-weighted average.

observations: Printed14 Binomial counts successes in independent Bernoulli trials; mass C(n,r)p^r(1−p)^(n−r). NLP example yes/no transitive-verb sentence trials. Gaussian is continuous with meanμ and standard deviationσ; density normalization and quadratic exponent shown. SLAM process noisev~N(0,V) andmeasurement noisew~N(0,W) used inKalman filter.
meaningfulAngles: Binomial trial assumptions, combinatorial factor and probability calculation.
Gaussian density parameters, shape and standard deviation versus variance.
Discrete count versus continuous-noise modeling and process/measurement noise distinction.

observations: Printed15 MLE uses observed data only; MAP incorporates prior. Posterior, likelihood, prior andevidence individually defined. Display chains MAP=argmax posterior=Bayes posterior fraction, conflating optimizing parameter with objective probability; proper argmax must cover the posterior expression. “Improves” is not guaranteed under a wrongprior.
meaningfulAngles: MLE versus MAP objectives and effect of prior.
Posterior/likelihood/prior/evidence roles; shared evidence drops out of model comparison.
MAP maximizing argument versus maximum probability value, and caveat on unconditional improvement.

observations: Printed16 Bayesian cycle prior→new sensor observation→posterior→new prior. Wall range sensor example contrasts latest-data MLE with measurement-plus-map-prior MAP. “More data becomes more accurate and stable” is a model-quality aspiration, not a deterministic guarantee for every sample.
meaningfulAngles: Sequential posterior-to-prior updating.
Wall-range example of MLE versus MAP and qualification of accuracy claims.

observations: Printed17 H(X)=−sum p(x)log2p(x), mean uncertainty/information; surprise wording; decision-tree impurity and informative features. “Better models…lower entropy” cannot be generalized to truth/correctness independent of calibration and distribution.
meaningfulAngles: Entropy formula, base2 units, normalization and zero-probability convention.
Uncertainty and decision-tree impurity comparisons, including pure versus balanced distributions.
Distinguish model confidence/low entropy from guaranteed correctness.

observations: Printed18 LTI state space: first-order model of input/output/state, converts higher-order equations to vector first order, multivariable robotics. xdot=Ax+Bu; y=Cx with no feedthrough term shown. Robot state may include position and velocity.
meaningfulAngles: State/input/output roles, equations and dimension-compatible matrix shapes.
Higher-order mechanical dynamics converted into a first-order state vector.
Evaluate a state derivative and output under the source no-feedthrough convention.

observations: Printed19 G=(V,E), node/edge roles, directed one-way versus undirected, weighted edge costs, paths andcycles; rooted directed acyclic tree wording is the lecture convention, not a universal restriction on all graph-theory trees. Path cost is sum of edge weights.
meaningfulAngles: Graph nodes/edges, direction and weight roles.
Path/cycle/tree distinctions with scope of rooted-directed convention.
Path cost as sum rather than hops alone.

observations: Printed20 Factory floor: docks as nodes, safe passages as edges, minimize traversal cost. Blue arrows show1→2(cost4),2→4(5),2→3(1),4→6(2). Green highlight1–3(2),3–5(3),5–6(1) totals6. Red dashed1–4 is blocked, not an extra zero-cost edge. Start blue ring atDock1, goalmagenta atDock6.
meaningfulAngles: Dock/passage graph semantics, start/goal and blocked-edge legend.
Compare legal path costs and recover highlighted minimum-cost route, not visually shortest blocked shortcut.

observations: Printed21 BFS: uninformed search lacks goal-location preference; level by edge count, FIFO queue, shortest number of edges not weighted cost. Figure highlights S–A–C–F–G with4 edges; alternative equal-length paths exist. Other edges include S–B,A–D,B–D,B–E,D–F,E–H,H–G. No neighbor order is specified.
meaningfulAngles: Uninformed versus goal-heuristic search.
BFS breadth/depth order and FIFO queue.
Fewest-edge optimality versus weighted cost and nonunique highlighted shortest path.

observations: Printed22 DFS explores deeply then backtracks, LIFO stack, often lower memory but no optimality guarantee. Red path S–A–C–F–D–B–E–H–G has8 edges, while blue shorter alternatives remain. It is a first-found example, not a uniquely determined trace without neighbor ordering.
meaningfulAngles: DFS depth/backtracking and LIFO.
First-found versus optimal path; compare highlighted DFS and BFS paths.
Memory-efficiency claim is conditional, not a universal speed guarantee.

observations: Printed23 calls the classification structure a search tree: internal attribute tests, branches outcomes, leaves decisions/classes. Sensor data maps to action/label. One decision tree is explicit rules; random forest combines many for robustness.
meaningfulAngles: Internal node/branch/leaf semantic roles and classification.
Decision tree versus random forest.

observations: Printed24 entropy repeated with information gain H(parent)−sum P(child)H(child), choose largest reduction to order questions. Tree: glass yes→fragile→low force; glass no→thickness; thick→high force, thin→low force. Explicit logic supports interpretability/safety/control, not guaranteed real-world correctness for all objects.
meaningfulAngles: Information gain weighted-child formula and split choice.
Full glass/thickness grasp-force decision-tree trace and outcomes.
Interpretability and explicit sensor-to-action rules.

observations: Printed25 asymptotic analysis counts T(n) growth, hardware-independent abstraction and dominant term. A=100n+1000 is linear; B=n²+1 quadratic. A eventually scales better despite constants, not necessarily at every smalln.
meaningfulAngles: Asymptotic versus measured runtime, highest-order term and growth classification.
Finite-size constants versus eventual scaling in supplied linear/quadratic example.

observations: Printed26 runtime operation count and worst/average cases, BFS fewest-edge optimality versus A* heuristic. Growth classes O(logn),O(n),O(n²). Euclidean-heuristic narrative says fewer nodes and ignores away directions; this is not a universal expansion bound or permission to prune every temporarily-away route.
meaningfulAngles: Operation-count runtime, worst versus average and growth-class comparisons.
BFS versus A* informed search; heuristic benefit versus universal efficiency claim and obstacle detours.

observations: Printed27 complete finds solution if one exists; source also says finite-time no-solution detection, requiring finite-search qualification. Resolution completeness relates to sufficiently fine discretization; probabilistic completeness approaches success probability1 as time grows. Genetic-algorithm example is conditional and distinct from finite-time optimality; blanket A* guarantee requires its assumptions.
meaningfulAngles: Complete, resolution-complete and probabilistically complete distinctions.
Completeness versus optimality and finite-time versus asymptotic guarantee.
Conditions needed for GA/A* claims rather than unconditional labels.

observations: Printed28 summary maps linear algebra to kinematics/dynamics/control; calculus to motion/velocity; probability to uncertain perception/localization/learning; state space; graph/search; complexity. SVD andchain rule are named only, with no decomposition or chain-rule derivation supplied on this page.
meaningfulAngles: Cross-topic matching of mathematical tools to robotics roles.
SVD and chain rule are name-only references, not source support for invented detailed derivations.
